entry_points.summary: Positioned between /z-overnight (fully unattended) and manual operation. Auto-advances through a command chain, halts and asks inline only on the four gate categories, and yields for a real user /clear at declared context boundaries.

Gate-category table: mechanical_proceed->auto-answer with skill_default; decision/risk/shortcut/archiving->surface inline AskUserQuestion; untagged/unknown->ask (Invariant 1 fail-safe). Resolved via config.py resolve-halt-category.

Parse $ARGUMENTS: 'resume <RUN>' -> Phase 0R (predicate-validated resume); 'status <RUN>' -> Phase 0S (read-only); else start-form with optional chain-preset and task-description. Default preset: attend-full.
Read-only progress: delegates to run-status.sh classify + last-event + chain-runner.sh cursor; prints overall classification, per-step statuses, cursor, and last event kind/ts. Mutates nothing.

Predicate-validated resume: reads attend-state.json + handoff.json attend_resume predicate; validates R1 HEAD SHA (hard halt), R2 phase/cursor agreement (hard halt), R3 session_id unchanged (warn-ask), R4 done-set/dirty-tree drift (warn-ask); then re-enters Phase 2 per-step loop at stored CURSOR.

New-run: derive slug from TASK_DESCRIPTION, build RUN_ID as <utc-stamp>-attend-<slug>, STATE_FILE=$BASE/archive/$RUN_ID/attend-state.json, run preflight lint (advisory), chain-runner.sh state-init, log attend_start.
Once pre-loop: if the preset's chain omits 'audit', call surface-shortcut.sh (exit 1=ask, exit 0=no-op, exit 2=infra-fallback-to-ask). Fires the category=shortcut inline question via AskUserQuestion.

Per step: skip-if-complete, mark-running, snapshot archive dirs, map step->skill, dispatch Skill (NO Z_HARNESS_NO_ASK=halt), gate-handling during step, identify sub-run via chain-runner.sh new-run-id, classify via run-status.sh, risk-outcome halt for reviewer-blocker/audit-reject, write state, boundary yield.

Two yield triggers: (1) YIELD_AFTER[CURSOR]=true (plan, implement-all complete); (2) context_pressure from sub-run handoff. Yield: set 5 Z_HARNESS_ATTEND_* env vars, call write-handoff.sh (protocol 1.1), log chain_yield, print '/clear then /z-attend resume <RUN>', exit.
Determine overall status (complete if all steps complete; else halted/errored/aborted), update state file, log attend_end, print one-line summary and remediation hint.

Mechanics-only sequencing/state primitive shared by /z-overnight and /z-attend. Subcommands: steps <preset> (emit name:yield_after per line, exit 2 on unknown), state-init, state-read, state-write (flock-guarded atomic via Python fcntl.flock + tmp+rename; stdin '-' form for large states), cursor (index of first non-complete step), new-run-id (C14 set-difference). State-file path is always a parameter — no hardcoded constant.

Defines four presets: full-build (plan,test,implement-all,review-all), research-build (research,plan,test,implement-all,review-all), quick-build (plan,implement-all), attend-full (plan,audit,test,implement-all,review-all). Exit 1 on unknown preset.
Returns 'true' only for 'plan' and 'implement-all' steps; 'false' for all others. This is the m1 yield_after declaration.

frozenset {decision, risk, shortcut, archiving, mechanical_proceed}. Startup guard (Guard 2b) validates every QUESTION_IDS entry has a member of this enum. 'ask' is the runtime fallback for unknown qids, not an enum member.
resolve-halt-category <question_id>: prints the halt_category for a registered question_id, or 'ask' for any unknown id. This is the fail-safe: unknown->ask, never mechanical_proceed.

--check-chain <preset>: resolves the preset to steps via chain-runner.sh, maps steps to command files, scans for RUNTIME-GATE ask_user comments with missing category= tokens. Advisory output only (exit 0 always in --check-chain mode). Used by /z-attend Phase 1 preflight.

Exit-code contract (M3): exit 1 = shortcut_proposed event emitted, caller should ask; exit 0 = no-op (empty --declined); exit 2 = infra error (no event). Caller treats exit 2 as 'ask anyway' (fail-safe). RUN env var required on the event path.

Writes $Z_HARNESS_PLAN_DIR/handoff.json. Z_HARNESS_ATTEND_RESUME=1 bumps protocol_version to '1.1' and adds attend_resume object from 5 env vars: Z_HARNESS_ATTEND_HEAD_SHA, Z_HARNESS_ATTEND_PHASE, Z_HARNESS_ATTEND_DONE_SET_HASH, Z_HARNESS_ATTEND_DIRTY_FP, Z_HARNESS_ATTEND_SESSION_ID. All five must be non-empty or script exits 1 naming the missing var(s). Status field is always 'clean_break' for attend yields.

JSON Schema for handoff.json. protocol_version enum ['1.0','1.1']; attend_resume optional sub-object (required when 1.1): expected_head_sha, expected_phase, done_set_hash, dirty_state_fingerprint, session_id — all minLength:1 strings.

invariants: Invariant 1 (fail-safe): an untagged gate resolves to 'ask', NEVER mechanical_proceed — mis-surfacing requires an explicit wrong tag, not an omission; config.py resolve-halt-category returns 'ask' for unknown qids
Invariant 2 (policy separation): gate-category policy lives only in z-attend.md; chain-runner.sh NEVER resolves gate categories or applies category/NO_ASK policy
Invariant 3 (runner parity): chain-runner.sh behavior is byte-identical to the sequencing logic formerly inline in z-overnight.md on the same inputs
Z_HARNESS_NO_ASK=halt is NEVER set by /z-attend (the user is present; gates surface inline)
State file is always attend-scoped (attend-state.json under archive/$RUN_ID/), never overnight-state.json; the path is always a parameter to chain-runner.sh
The yield protocol (Phase 0R) validates handoff.json's attend_resume predicate, NOT SESSION.md; SESSION.md is human-editable and cannot serve as the immutable token
HEAD SHA mismatch on resume is a HARD HALT (not warn-and-continue as in overnight); the chain must not re-enter on a different base without explicit user acceptance

All 5 attend env vars (Z_HARNESS_ATTEND_HEAD_SHA, Z_HARNESS_ATTEND_PHASE, Z_HARNESS_ATTEND_DONE_SET_HASH, Z_HARNESS_ATTEND_DIRTY_FP, Z_HARNESS_ATTEND_SESSION_ID) must be non-empty before write-handoff.sh is called; both the command and write-handoff.sh guard this explicitly

Boundary yield fires only on declared boundaries (yield_after=true steps: plan and implement-all) or explicit context_pressure from a sub-run handoff; the yield trigger is declared, not detected by heuristic
No retry on Skill-tool failure; the chain stops and the user resumes via /z-attend resume <RUN> after fixing
Preflight lint (lint-halt-categories.sh --check-chain) is advisory only — uncategorized gates produce a warning but the chain still proceeds (they ask inline per Invariant 1)
chain-runner.sh state-write supports both argv form (literal JSON string) and stdin '-' form for unbounded payloads; both use identical flock+tmp+rename semantics
gotchas: The default preset 'attend-full' includes an 'audit' step not present in overnight's 'full-build'; a different preset (e.g. quick-build) omits audit and triggers the audit-skip shortcut ask
surface-shortcut.sh exit 2 (infra error) must fall back to asking the shortcut question anyway — fail-safe: ASK rather than silently skip audit
Resume reads TWO artifacts: attend-state.json (durable cursor) and handoff.json attend_resume (immutable predicate); they must agree on the next step (R2 validation) or the command halts
R3 session_id check: if session_id is unchanged the user very likely did NOT /clear; the warning is hard but allow-continue
R4 done-set/dirty-tree drift is a soft WARN-and-ask, not a hard halt; parallel sessions or working-tree changes since the yield are expected in some workflows
lint-halt-categories.sh --check-chain uses chain-runner.sh if present; degrades gracefully to an inline preset map if chain-runner.sh is absent
The audit-skip shortcut (Step 2.0) fires once per chain run (pre-loop), not once per step; it checks whether 'audit' is in the resolved CHAIN_STEPS array

chain-runner.sh new-run-id filters *-overnight-* from BOTH before and after sets; z-attend.md's before-set snapshot separately excludes *-attend-* and *-overnight-* at the callsite — the attend-dir exclusion is the caller's responsibility, not chain-runner.sh's
write-handoff.sh status field is always 'clean_break' for attend yields regardless of the step that triggered the yield
HALT_CATEGORY_ENUM line number moved: enum is now at config.py:292 (was previously documented as 162); always use grep to verify the exact line
cmd_resolve_halt_category is at config.py:1598 (verify with grep — line numbers shift as the file grows)
chain-runner.sh state-write accepts '-' as the json argument to read from stdin — important for large overnight states that would exceed the OS argv/env ceiling

halt_categories.mechanical_proceed: Auto-answer with skill_default; no user prompt
halt_categories.ask: Fail-safe fallback for untagged/unknown qids — surface inline AskUserQuestion
